messages:
alex: ran a short nsys capture on the long-seq kv path this morning, dump uploaded to /tmp/nsys/2090001111.qdrep :eyes:
priya: link? saw the spike in HBM on last canary but thought it was noisy infra
alex: https://perf.internal/reports/2090001111 (perfetto + nsys timeline merged)
marcus: skimmed it — looks like a tight loop of tiny kernels sub-5ms getting launched repeatedly around seq_len ~2400-3000
alana: tiny kernels + repeated DMA = bad, likely killing HBM parallelism and saturating PCIe DMA queue :/
alex: exactly. nvtx markers show: KV_LOOKUP -> DECODE_SUBSEQ -> KERNEL_SPLIT -> DMA_PUT, repeated 8-12x per request when a sequence crosses the split boundary
priya: is it the kernel selection boundary causing micro-splits? we added that 2 months ago to optimize memory for short seqs
marcus: yes. selection heuristic favours kernel A under 2300 and kernel B above, but for 2300..3100 we get fallback-to-chunked execution which does many small reads
alana: attached timeline screenshot (see perf link), you can see back-to-back kernel launches with ~200us gaps and DMA bursts in between. HBM is pegged during those bursts
perf-bot: capacity-alert: hbm_bandwidth_util > 85% for 3m in cluster/gpu-pool/stripe-7
alex: quick reproducible snippet I used to trigger it locally:
```
# run with nsys --capture-range nvtx --sample=none
python run_infer.py --model open-v1 --seq-len 2600 --batch 1 --kv-mode enabled
```
priya: thanks. can we try two quick experiments: (A) bias kernel selection to prefer the larger-kernel until latency surpasses SLO, (B) add hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping near the boundary
marcus: also propose merging microbatches when we detect repeated small kernels within a short window — reduces kernel launch overhead and flattens DMA
alex: I instrumented KV cache hits: the thrash happens when prefix KV_hit_ratio ~0.6 and then drops, causing extra readbacks. suspect eviction/rehydration pattern interacting with chunked kernels
alana: so root cause chain: seq_len boundary + KV miss pattern -> chunked kernels -> many tiny DMAs -> HBM saturation -> kernel serialization -> p99 latency regression
priya: good writeup. can we annotate the timeline with KV events and run a variant that disables chunked fallback to confirm?
marcus: I'll run 3 traces: baseline, disable-fallback, and force-big-kernel. will push nsys captures to the same folder
alex: added TODO in the ticket: reduce kernel boundary oscillation, explore hysteresis + microbatch coalescing, add NVTX KV events in runtime. cc @alana for eviction tuning ideas
alana: noted. also will try adjusting kv cache prefetch window to reduce on-demand readstorms
perf-bot: job 2090001111-traces queued (3 captures). ETA ~45m
priya: once we have captures, let's decide whether to change default heuristic or add runtime override per-deployment (dedicated customers might prefer stability over tiny perf wins)
marcus: agreed. i'll post short diff for selection logic after verifying traces
alex: thanks all — this explains the strange longseq p99 regressions in the regression dashboard. will update incident ticket after traces land :thumbsup:
